_comment: All tunable knobs live here. Change weights/thresholds without touching code.

model._comment: Semantic model and additive advisor artifact schema versions. Every published JSON artifact receives this version plus the producing git SHA, full settings hash, and generation timestamp.

filing_extraction._comment: Off by default. pipeline/filing_extraction.py parses 8-K Exhibit 99.x earnings releases for operating KPIs (same-store sales, NIM, ARPU, etc.) that are not standardized XBRL facts -- but it has NOT been validated against a single live SEC EDGAR fetch (see that module's docstring for why: this session's sandbox blocked sec.gov). A human must confirm its extraction against real filings and check minimum_coverage is actually cleared before setting enabled to true. Even once enabled, every reading is tagged unaudited and stays out of the scored composite, same as reverse_dcf and the new sector metrics above.

reverse_dcf._comment: Declared assumptions for pipeline/reverse_dcf.py's single-stage market-implied-growth read (Mauboussin & Rappaport reverse DCF), not fitted or fetched figures -- same 'labeled, not measured' honesty pipeline/costs.py applies to its spread proxy. risk_free_rate/equity_risk_premium feed a CAPM cost of equity; default_cost_of_debt is a flat pre-tax assumption since actual borrowing cost is not fetched per company; implausible_growth_ceiling flags a solved growth rate no perpetuity should sustain rather than asserting a specific fair value. This is informational only -- not part of the scored composite -- pending its own ic_harness.py read.

cross_sectional_normalization._comment: The live champion remains on bands. The challenger fits metric distributions on the complete refreshed universe and publishes beside it. Valuation own-history percentiles use only prospectively stored observations from the trailing five years and remain unavailable until twelve distinct dated observations exist.

signal_corrections._comment: The cumulative challenger applies data-coverage shrinkage once and expresses every modifier allocation as a fraction of the combined cap. Its short-horizon treatment is 'reversal' rather than 'neutral' now that the champion is neutral: with both set to neutral the variant was identical to the champion and the comparison tested nothing. Reversal asks the open question -- whether short-horizon relative strength carries contrarian information -- at the reduced reversal_weight.

confidence._comment: Decomposes the single confidence scalar (weighted fundamental/technical/news coverage, see scorer.weighted_coverage) into the components docs/RESEARCH-CONTRACT.md's confidence redesign calls for. This is additive: it does not change the score, the champion formula, or the existing 'confidence' field -- it publishes a confidence_detail breakdown alongside it so a low score can be explained ('why') rather than just observed.

validation._horizons_days_comment: Calendar-day horizons: secondary diagnostics only. horizons_sessions below is the preregistered primary target (B1) -- real trading sessions from public/data/etf/SPY.json, not calendar time.
validation._comment: Prospective point-in-time validation only. Headline statistics stay hidden until the configured monthly history gate is met.

position_risk._comment: Position decisions reference the highest observed close since purchase. Cost basis remains display-only.

watchlist_setup._comment: Watchlist quality is a weighted geometric mean of continuous thesis, research, data coverage, and published-guidance subscores. Only data coverage below the hard floor or a published Sell blocks sizing. Equal-risk sizing scales each name against the calmest covered name and retains the same per-name cap.

watchlist_price_targets._comment: Suggested entry levels for a watchlist name the user does not yet own -- both are explicit heuristics, not predictions, and every result states its own derivation so the number is never presented as more certain than it is. dip_buy is a volatility-scaled distance below the current price (the same ATR/sigma-scaling philosophy as position_risk's stop-loss levels, but anchored to current price since a watchlist name has no purchase high-water-mark). good_buy is a valuation-percentile-based discount: only applies a discount when the name is priced richer than its own configured fair percentile against sector/industry peers (peer_groups.py desirability_percentile, where higher = cheaper) -- a name already cheap relative to peers gets good_buy == current price rather than an invented discount.

acceleration._comment: Portfolio-level acceleration against the benchmark (src/lib/portfolioAcceleration.js): beta-adjusted excess return over the most recent leg_days, less the same over the leg_days before it, divided by the portfolio's own tracking noise. Beta-adjusting is what separates a portfolio that outran the index from one the index carried; dividing by tracking noise makes the reading comparable across a concentrated book and a diversified one. leg_days is a calendar quarter rather than 63 trading sessions because the portfolio value series is not guaranteed to be daily. skip_days drops the last week, where short-term reversal lives. Same measure as market_behavior.relative_acceleration, which does this per company on daily closes.

benchmark_comparison._comment: Up/down capture and batting average (src/lib/portfolioBenchmarkComparison.js). Capture splits the record by which way the index went, because a single blended ratio cannot distinguish a portfolio that wins by keeping up in rallies from one that wins by losing less in selloffs - opposite portfolios with the same Sharpe. Batting average is bucketed by calendar month rather than by observation: a hit rate is meaningless without a stated cadence, and monthly makes it independent of how densely the value series happens to be sampled.

short_term_view._comment: Fast benchmark-relative reads (src/lib/portfolioShortTermView.js) for the horizons the quarter- and year-scale measures cannot speak to, and for accounts too new for them. Short windows are mostly noise, so every window is published beside a noise floor - one standard error of this portfolio's own tracking noise over a window of that length - and a reading inside the floor is labelled as such rather than reported as a result. Windows report independently: three weeks of history answers the week and honestly declines the month. Beta for the adjustment is fitted over baseline_days rather than the short window itself, so a one-week reading is not adjusted by a one-week beta; below minimum_intervals_for_beta the excess falls back to a plain difference and says so.

shortTermExcessPct._comment: Deliberately wide. A short-horizon excess return is mostly noise, and colouring a +0.4% week green would tell the reader it means something. The tile only takes a tone once the move clears its own noise floor, and these bounds keep even that conservative.

longestUnderwaterDays._comment: Fewer days underwater is better, and tone bounds are read as higher-is-better, so the tile passes the negated day count as its tone value: two months or less underwater reads good, nine months or more reads bad. Up and down capture carry no bounds on purpose - neither is good or bad without the other half, which is what captureSpread scores.

portfolio_analytics._comment: Modified Dietz weights settled external flows by time invested. Correlation analytics use trailing daily total-price returns. The diversification score gives half its weight to effective bets and the diversification ratio, with the other half calibrated from HHI concentration. Performance metric tones use configured good minimums and bad maximums. Values between those boundaries remain neutral, and drawdowns are better when they are closer to zero.

etf_lookthrough._comment: ETF sector weights and the largest published underlying positions are retained from the existing free Yahoo fund snapshot. Unreported residual weight remains explicit rather than being assigned to a synthetic holding.

factor_data._comment: Official monthly US research factors from the Ken French Data Library. The cache refreshes at most monthly and publishes percentage returns as decimal values.

anomaly_rules.message: Operating margin is declining while revenue is still growing quickly. This divergence often signals that incremental growth is becoming less profitable.
Accruals are elevated while free cash flow growth trails earnings growth. This pattern can indicate weaker cash conversion of reported earnings.
Days sales outstanding is extending while revenue growth is nonpositive. This pattern can indicate slower customer collections.
Buyback yield is positive while net debt to EBITDA is elevated. This combination means repurchases are occurring alongside meaningful leverage.

explainability._comment: Attribution starts from a neutral 50 and reconciles exactly through evidence, confidence, and every modifier. Anomaly messages describe observed rule-based divergences and never predict outcomes.

alerts._comment: Rules always create in-app events. Push is an optional enhancement, repeated active conditions are deduplicated, and quiet hours suppress delivery without suppressing the in-app event.

projection._comment: Projection paths resample consecutive 12-month blocks to preserve short-run return dependence. The dotted median is centered on the user's adjustable annual return target, which defaults to 15 percent. Supplied brokerage returns define an evidence range when available but do not silently replace the target. Once there is enough daily history to compute Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar (the same gate the Overview panel uses), the model draws from a distribution calibrated to those ratios instead, refreshed weekly at Friday market close (America/New_York) or on a new deposit-like activity, whichever comes first. With less history than that, the model uses observed portfolio returns after the 36-month gate, or the selected benchmark's full monthly history recentered on the target. Observed months are never repeated or synthesized. Allocation scenarios change dispersion around the target.

interface._comment: Presentation constants shared by the responsive report and confidence-encoded research score dial. Confidence controls arc opacity and dash density while the research score controls arc length. Preview positions are available only behind the development-only portfolioPreview screenshot query.

fundamentals._comment: Fundamental score: sector-aware valuation plus profitability, balance-sheet health, cash generation, growth, capital allocation, and accounting quality. Percentages are decimals (15% = 0.15). Weights follow the strength of the published evidence for each signal, not the convenience of the data: EV/EBITDA and gross profitability carry weight because Loughran-Wellman and Novy-Marx measured them working; PEG and the accruals ratio carry little because their support is thin or has decayed.
fundamentals._extended_comment: Quality, capital-allocation, and accounting-integrity bands. Trends are decimal fractions; ratios are multiples.

altman_z._comment: Distress/safe cutoffs differ by variant. z is Altman's original 1968 manufacturing model (distress <1.81, safe >2.99); z_double_prime is his non-manufacturer revision on a different scale (distress <1.1, safe >2.6). Financials are suppressed entirely.

asset_growth._comment: Investment factor: conservative asset growth beats aggressive. Shrinkage is not rewarded above steady reinvestment, so this is a range, not a floor.

modifiers._comment: Bounded adjustments applied after the evidence blend. They refine, never replace, the evidence score. Units are score points.

macro_regime._comment: FRED-derived context is a sector-sensitive modifier, never a primary ranking factor.

insider_activity._comment: SEC Form 4 open-market activity scored via the Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski (JF 2012) routine-versus-opportunistic split. Routine calendar-scheduled trades score zero - the paper finds their returns are essentially zero. Opportunistic cluster buys earn up to max_points and decay over one to three months, the horizon the effect pays off over. Sells are capped lower because insiders sell for many non-informative reasons.

customer_concentration_risk._comment: ASC 280 customer concentration read from dimensional XBRL (pipeline/concentration_risk.py) - a known, penalty-only risk, not a bet on direction. Below warning_share scores zero; at or above it, half the max penalty; at or above severe_share, the full penalty. SHADOW MODE ONLY (apply_challenger_modifiers, not apply_modifiers) until ConcentrationRiskPercentage1 tagging coverage across the scored universe is measured on a live run - see capability_status.customer_concentration_risk.

geographic_concentration._comment: Single-country revenue concentration read from dimensional XBRL (pipeline/geographic_exposure.py), same shape as customer_concentration_risk. Only fires on concentration in one non-domestic geography, not on international revenue in general. SHADOW MODE ONLY (apply_challenger_modifiers, not apply_modifiers): geographic revenue tags often reflect shipping destination or contracting entity rather than end demand and need spot-checking - see capability_status.fx_exposure.

institutional_13f._comment: Breadth of curated, publicly traded, style=active-only asset managers' quarter-over-quarter 13F position change (pipeline/institutional_ownership.py, pipeline/build_institutional_screen.py). Two-sided like insider_activity: requires min_managers net movers on one side before it scores anything. half_life_days/max_age_days decay the magnitude by how stale the underlying filing already is - a 13F position is disclosed up to 45 days after quarter-end, so it is never fully current; a filing older than max_age_days scores zero rather than being read as still-current. Read from the monthly-refreshed published screen, not fetched live per advisor run.

congressional_buying._comment: Disclosed Congressional stock purchases (pipeline/congress_signal.py), reward-only. Explicit, scoped exception to the 'no political inputs' principle stated in advisor_engine.py's module docstring - see that docstring and TODO.md for what was declined (scoring congressional holdings as evidence a stock/sector is politically protected from failure) versus what shipped (breadth x freshness of disclosed purchases, with a bonus for EXTRAORDINARY_BUY: a member's first-ever trade in a sub-$2B company). Reads the weekly-published congress screen, not a live fetch. Evidentiary basis: Ziobrowski et al. (JFQA 2004, and the 2011 House companion study) find abnormal returns to disclosed Congressional purchases in pre-STOCK-Act samples; whether that survives the post-2012 mandatory-disclosure regime is untested here.

filing_8k._comment: 8-K Item-code materiality (pipeline/edgar_filing_signals.py), classified from SEC's own item taxonomy - never parsed from filing text. Penalty-only: bankruptcy, restatement, delisting, impairment, accelerated debt, exit costs, auditor change, and dilutive unregistered sales each carry a documented negative reading; nothing on Form 8-K is scored positive, since no item code reliably means good news the way these reliably mean bad. Only the single freshest qualifying filing is scored. Reads the 3-day-published SEC filings screen, not a live fetch.

proxy_signal._comment: Contested proxy elections (DEFC14A form code, pipeline/edgar_filing_signals.py) - an unambiguous governance conflict. Penalty-only. Additional soliciting material (DEFA14A) is published as a flag but never scored: the form code alone can't separate a genuine activist situation from routine solicitation updates. Reads the 3-day-published SEC filings screen, not a live fetch.

filing_integrity._comment: Late 10-K/10-Q notification (NT 10-K/NT 10-Q form code, pipeline/edgar_filing_signals.py) - a well-documented distress or accounting-problem signal on its own. Penalty-only; an on-time 10-K/10-Q carries no score signal by itself. Reads the 3-day-published SEC filings screen, not a live fetch.

bucket_weights._comment: The valuation input is the broad fundamental score (valuation, profitability, health, and growth).

build._comment: The Firestore client is split below the 500 kB advisory ceiling with headroom for dependency growth.

labels._comment: Composite score -> label. Never 'BUY'. Research candidates only.

ranking_weights._comment: Blend of the three evidence components. Fundamentals dominate by design. News sentiment is a 4% tilt rather than a 10% component because headline alpha decays within days (Tetlock 2007); the freed weight went to market behavior, which is now built on 12-1 momentum and real Sharpe/Sortino rather than invented constants.

news_intelligence._comment: News remains a 4% tilt. Articles are filtered by entity confidence, deduplicated by title similarity, and weighted by exponential recency, source quality, and whether the item is a source-of-record filing or commentary.

event_type_markers._comment: Keyword classification (brief section 15) -- deterministic and title/source-based, same approach as content_type/source_quality above. A headline can match multiple types; classify_event_type returns every match, ordered by this dict's key order, so the caller decides how to prioritize rather than this function silently picking one.

market_behavior._comment: Market-behavior sub-weights, using the same risk math as the ETF model so a Sharpe means the same thing on both screens. momentum_12_1 skips the most recent month to avoid short-term reversal (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993); low_beta rewards defensive names per betting-against-beta (Frazzini-Pedersen 2014) instead of penalizing volatility with a hand-tuned constant. technical_extended (pipeline/technical_indicators.py) is deliberately small. relative_strength is listed here but excluded from the champion blend by short_horizon_treatment='neutral': it is computed as ret_20d minus a benchmark return that is the same scalar for every row, so it is rank-identical to return_20d by construction (Spearman +1.00 across 877 published rows) and was drawing 16% of this blend for a signal already present. See research/audit/CURRENT_MODEL_AUDIT.md section 6.

relative_acceleration._comment: Whether a name's market-relative pace is picking up: cumulative beta-adjusted excess return over the most recent leg_days sessions, minus the same over the leg immediately before it, divided by its own standard error (risk_metrics.relative_acceleration). Beta-adjusting is what makes it genuinely market-relative rather than a relabelled own-return - a raw stock-minus-index difference subtracts the same scalar from every row and cannot change a cross-sectional ranking, which is the section 6 audit finding against relative_strength above. skip_days drops the most recent week because that is where short-term reversal lives, the same reason momentum_12_1 skips a month. This block has NO entry in weights and does not reach the score: it is published for the validation harness to measure prospectively, and should only be promoted to a weight if that measurement supports one. Basis: Gettleman & Marks (2006) on acceleration, Blitz-Huij-Martens (2011) on residual construction.

evidence_events._comment: Event-level evidence weights. Every number here is a starting prior chosen from the published literature and ordinary market experience, NOT a measured constant - they are frozen deliberately so the point-in-time store accumulates observations under one fixed policy, and they should only move when walk-forward evidence supports it. Half-lives are in TRADING days: an event that lands on Friday must not have burned two half-lives by Monday open.

event_materiality._comment: How much a headline of this kind can move an expected cash-flow path, 0-1. This is what stops a +0.95-sentiment 'best places to work' award from outranking a +0.75-sentiment guidance raise. Highest matched type wins (see event_materiality).

event_half_life_trading_days._comment: How long this kind of information stays live. Strategic and regulatory outcomes resolve slowly and keep repricing; ordinary commentary is stale within a session or two. Longest matched type wins, because the slowest-resolving element of a story is what keeps it relevant.

insider_half_life_trading_days._comment: Far slower than news, and deliberately so. Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski measure the opportunistic-insider effect over roughly one to three months, so a purchase is still informative weeks later - decaying it on a news schedule would throw away the signal.

expectation_weights._comment: Analyst conviction is about CHANGE, not level: a static 2.6/5 consensus is already in the price. Recommendation changes accompanied by estimate revisions are the ones that provoke drift, so revision breadth and magnitude carry most of the weight.

evidence_events._saturation_comment: Signed event strengths are summed and squashed through tanh rather than averaged. An average divides materiality straight back out (the average of one trivial event is that event), and an unbounded sum would let the most-covered company run away with the screen.

headline_direction_markers._comment: Yahoo's news feed carries no sentiment score at all, so direction is derived from these phrases over the headline and summary - a deterministic keyword match in the same style as event_type_markers, NOT a sentiment model, and it should be read that way. Only the strongest matching phrase is used (headlines are short; summing lets three mild words outvote one decisive one), and a headline matching nothing carries no direction at all rather than a fabricated neutral. Weights are signed magnitudes in [-1, 1]: the extremes are reserved for statements that directly restate an expected cash-flow path.

data_health._comment: Round 4 provider-health monitoring and publication gate (docs/AUDIT-ROUND-4-FINDINGS.md). Statement coverage is measured per refresh against monitored_metrics; below degraded_below the refresh is labeled degraded, below critical_below critical, and the run manifest carries the state. min_publication_coverage is the per-name floor: a research score computed from less than this fraction of intended fundamentals weight publishes as INSUFFICIENT DATA rather than a ranked stance, because Round 3 item 4 measured identical evidence scoring up to 1.87x apart on data availability alone.
